---
title: "Cross-linguistic generalisation of the prosodic hierarchy: cortical entrainment to Italian speech"
date: 2026-04-01
description: >
  Does the level-selective cortical entrainment pattern established for German, where
  phase-amplitude coupling tracks a top-down structure from intonational phrase to foot to
  syllable, also appear in Italian? An EEG study with about 30 Italian L1 listeners uses a
  parallel Italian stimulus set to ask whether a language with a different constraint
  ranking shows the same entrainment hierarchy. Master thesis.
image: assets/prosodic-hierarchy-italian.jpg
categories: [Neuroscience, Psycholinguistics]
---

Master thesis at the Institute for the Interdisciplinary Study of Language Evolution (ISLE), University
of Zürich. Supervised by Prof. Dr. Martin Meyer (UZH) and Prof. Dr. Stefan Debener (Oldenburg), in
collaboration with PD Dr. Elisa Pellegrino.

**Why Italian.** It shares the core prosodic architecture of German (free lexical stress, a full
prosodic hierarchy, focus encoded through prominence) but ranks the constraints differently: German
prioritises rhythmic regularity, Italian prioritises focus-driven phrasing. A difference in
entrainment would therefore point to language-specific constraint ranking shaping how a shared
hierarchical mechanism is expressed.

**Design.** Purely neural (EEG), with audio-motor synchronisation as a modular predictor of individual
differences. The core analysis is pairwise phase consistency in the theta, high delta and low delta
bands, modelled with glmertree, with phase-amplitude coupling as an extension.
